title: 6th Annual Applied Value Investing Stock Pitch Challenge
description: The 6th Annual Applied Value Investing Stock Pitch Challenge featuring the work for Value Investing Program students Morgan Zhang '25 - AO Smith  (first place), Mario Stefanidis - '25 CNH (second place), Harsha Mohan '25 - Global Payments, and Kit Popolo '25 – Ibotta, and presented by sponsors Artisan International Value, Summit Street Capital Management and CP&E Partners.
summary: The primary argument focuses on Global Payments (GPN) as a compelling investment opportunity driven by depressed valuations and a shift in management strategy under CEO Cameron Brady. The speaker contends that the company is successfully executing a capital allocation plan to return $7.5 billion to shareholders over three years, primarily through share repurchases rather than acquisitions, which should be accretive even if organic growth stagnates. While other payment processors like Fiserv are mentioned for context regarding market share and digital migration, the core bullish thesis is reserved for GPN's specific turnaround potential and shareholder-friendly capital deployment.

claims.claim: The speaker believes investing in Global Payments offers mid-teens returns due to depressed valuations, competent management, and a focus on shareholder capital allocation.
claims.quote: In conclusion, I believe being long Global Payments today offers an opportunity to earn mid-teens returns by investing at depressed valuations in a competent top five player, which is managed to prove that it's here to stay aided by a management team, which is now focusing on making capital allocation decisions, which help shareholders not just the top line, along with levers that they can prove to the market, that they can execute on the strategy even if the market doesn't believe them.

claims.claim: Global Payments has successfully grown revenues, EPS, and operating margins while maintaining market share and adapting to the digital landscape.
claims.quote: During the same time period, global Payments has not only managed to grow revenues by 18% and adjusted EPS by 40%, but also expanded adjusted operating margins by 500 basis points while my while maintaining its market share of transactions amongst legacy players.

claims.claim: The company is not plateauing and has sustained double-digit growth in its e-commerce segment, contradicting bear theses about it being an obsolete legacy player.
claims.quote: So they're nowhere close to plateauing out on their ability to grow while focusing on this slice of customer. Also, contrary to the Bear thesis, the e-commerce segment within Merchant Solutions has sustained double digit growth rates. Lending validation to my thesis that Global Payments is not an obsolete legacy player incapable of adapting with the times.

claims.claim: Management plans to return $7.5 billion in cash to shareholders over three years, reducing share count by about 20%, a strategy the speaker believes is feasible.
claims.quote: Secondly, management has outlined a plan to return $7.5 billion in cash to shareholders over the next three years, which I estimate should reduce share count by about 20%. The company has $3 billion of cash on the balance sheet, a a five year high compared to the historical $2 billion average. And its business operations currently generate about two to two and a half billion dollars in lever free cash flow. And it's poised to improve, which makes me believe that this strategy is feasible to execute.

claims.claim: The current CEO, Cameron Brady, has prioritized share repurchases over acquisitions, showing a different strategy than the former CEO Jeff Sloan.
claims.quote: The current CEO Cameron Brady has clearly stated that he plans to limit acquisitions and prioritize share repurchases. And over the past 18 months, he has shown that he will not put your money where Jeff's mouth was. Global Payments has made no major acquisitions since June, 2023, and in fact, they've divested non-core verticals to streamline the business from 2021 to 2023.

claims.claim: Since taking over in June 2023, the percentage of capital deployed towards M&A has shrunk from 45% to 20%, while capital for share repurchases has increased.
claims.quote: About 45% of their capital deployed was towards m and a since Mr. Brady took over in June 23. That number has shrunk to 20%, along with an increase in the percentage of capital deployed towards Share Repurchases.

claims.quote: So to the extent that this cash can be deployed over the next 18 months, I think that can still reflect in the stock price, even if they manage, even if they go back to their old roots and make an acquisition sometime in the future.
